heroHeadline: FDA Approves Zenbexus (Iberdomide), First-Ever CELMoD Therapy, in Historic First Oncology Approval Based Directly on MRD Endpoint — Days After Gladstone/UCSF Team Unveils Gene Edits That Supercharge CAR-T Against Solid Tumors
heroSubtitle: On August 13, 2026, the FDA granted accelerated approval to Bristol Myers Squibb's Zenbexus (iberdomide) plus daratumumab/dexamethasone for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma — the first-ever approved cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD) and the first oncology drug in history approved directly on minimal residual disease (MRD)-negative complete response as a surrogate endpoint (41% vs. 21% for control, p<0.0001), ahead of confirmatory progression-free survival data. One day earlier, a Gladstone Institutes/UCSF team led by Julia Carnevale and Alex Marson published in Nature the first in vivo genome-wide CRISPR screen performed inside living tumors, identifying two gene edits (P2RY8 and GNAS deletion) that let CAR-T cells overcome the immunosuppressive solid-tumor microenvironment — two-thirds of treated mice remained tumor-free versus zero with unedited CAR-T. The results build on a summer that included FDA approval of Replimune's Tudriqev oncolytic virus for anti-PD-1-resistant melanoma (Aug 6) and Pluvicto's expansion into earlier-stage prostate cancer (Jul 31).
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA Drug Approvals, NIH/NCI, peer-reviewed journals (NEJM, The Lancet, JCO, Nature, Nature Medicine), ASCO/ESMO/AACR conference data, and institutional analyses. All clinical data reflect published and presented trial results.
